name: Linear
verdict: Self-serve: create an OAuth app in Settings → Administration → API, with no mandatory review, in about 1-3 days. Agent installs need a workspace admin, and a Third-Party App Approvals feature may gate your app.
needGuide: Short one, but expect a workspace admin to install actor=app agents.

auth.detail: Authorization code with optional PKCE (S256 or plain; client_secret becomes optional with PKCE). Access tokens last 24 hours; refresh tokens rotate (30-minute replay grace) and all apps were migrated to refresh tokens on 2026-04-01. actor=app installs the app as its own user (agent). Client-credentials grant (30-day app tokens) is available if enabled on the app.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review); directory listing timeline unknown

approval.gate: No mandatory review to let other workspaces authorize. An actor=app install needs a workspace admin. Listing in Linear's Integration Directory is by submission (process not retrieved). Linear also has a 'Third-Party App Approvals' admin feature (page not retrieved), so customer admins may gate your app.

scopes.why: read by default plus a few narrow write scopes; customer and initiative scopes are separate opt-ins.
scopes.summary: read (default), write, issues:create, comments:create, timeSchedule:write, admin (not allowed with actor=app), app:assignable, app:mentionable, customer:read/write, initiative:read/write. Request only narrow scopes. Customer and initiative scopes are separate opt-ins.

cost: Free (agent development is free; installed agents are not billable users)
prerequisites: Account and owner: A workspace admin must create the OAuth app. Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for managing the app because every admin in that workspace can see it and its secrets.
Where you register: Settings → Administration → API → OAuth applications → Create new (admin permission needed to see the page)
Cost: Free (agent development is free; installed agents are not billable users)

registerAt.path: Settings → Administration → API → OAuth applications → Create new (admin permission needed to see the page)

steps.do: Create a dedicated Linear workspace owned by a company account to host the app
Open Settings → Administration → API and create an OAuth application with callback URLs, name and icon
Enable webhooks (Agent session events, Permission changes) if building an agent; enable client credentials only for internal automation
Implement authorize URL with actor=app, scope list (read, write, app:assignable, app:mentionable) and PKCE; exchange the code and store the refresh token
Record the per-workspace app ID (viewer { id }) next to the stored token
Install into a second test workspace as its admin and verify delegation, mentions and revoke handling
Submit to the Integration Directory if you want public listing

roles.team: A workspace admin must create the OAuth app. Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for managing the app because every admin in that workspace can see it and its secrets.
roles.console: No per-app collaborators documented; access is every admin of the owning workspace.
roles.customer: A workspace admin must install an actor=app agent (workspace-scoped). Admins can later change or revoke the app's team access; admins can also disable member API-key creation. Possible approval gate via Third-Party App Approvals (unconfirmed).

testing: Create a free dedicated Linear workspace, make the OAuth app there, and install it with actor=app into the same or a second test workspace.
Agents must emit a 'thought' activity within 10 seconds of a session starting.

blockers.fix: Give prospects an admin-ready install link and explanation.

blockers.problem: Admin scope cannot combine with actor=app
blockers.fix: Use narrower scopes or a separate user-actor flow.
Use the 30-minute replay grace after network errors and store the newest token.

blockers.problem: Customer admins may restrict third-party apps via approvals or team-access limits

automation.agentCan: Cannot create the app in the UI, but can write the OAuth/refresh code, webhook handlers, agent-session logic, directory submission copy, and an admin install guide, and run test GraphQL calls.
automation.humanMust: Admin sign-in to create the app, secrets handling, any directory submission contact, and customer-admin approval of installs.

uncertain: Whether Linear OAuth apps have a public/private toggle, the Third-Party App Approvals behavior, and the Integration Directory submission process were not confirmed (pages failed to fetch).
